checks.check: Anonymous lifecycle overview is denied
Overview separates read-only shared catalog and disables purge
Reviewed PNG explains immutable review and queued package retention
Selected package explains pins, retained artwork and pipeline history
Foreign origin cannot mutate lifecycle
Stale document binding cannot mutate lifecycle
Wrong media type cannot mutate lifecycle
Strict target/schema/body boundaries reject malformed and oversized commands without mutation
Pin then archive preserves the exact reviewed Pixi pin
New instance automatic artwork selection skips archived package
Archive before explicit pin blocks new selection
Exact archive retry is idempotent
Old request replay after restore never reapplies archive
Concurrent same-revision archive commands admit exactly one transaction
Stale unpin never clears a concurrent replacement
Unpin replay and stale undo preserve a later pin
Archived original blocks dependent package selection without making reviewed bytes eligible
Archived file rejects new package but retains exact already-admitted queue retry
Job admitted before archive can finish source processing while history remains retained
Archived dependency fences undo, old yard backup, package and shape admission
Restored dependency permits exact pin undo and the same valid shape request
Archived conditioning reference blocks new derivation while existing PNG pin resolves
Concurrent pin and archive preserve one valid transaction order
Only unreviewed unreferenced archived upload is cleanup-eligible and all bytes remain
Restore cancels cleanup eligibility
Foreign owner cannot inspect, archive, unpin or reuse another owner's receipt
Public yard excludes private lifecycle, file identity, review and command receipts
Lost-response retry survives tab navigation and keyboard activation with the exact original command

coverageLimits: Transaction failpoints and disposable byte purge are separate storage unit tests.
HTTP races cover same-revision CAS and both deterministic pin/archive serial orders; repository tests cover separate database connections.
